player_0.content: New plan: My previous attempt failed because I assigned a high score to "Justified" without fully analyzing the character's defensive posture and the specific context of the final line. Grayson's closing statement ("At least I'm not lying to the public") is a defensive deflection used to counter Dr. Sinclair's accusation of being a "sensationalist," rather than a genuine expression of triumph or deep-seated justification. I incorrectly interpreted his stubbornness as confidence. Next time, I will re-evaluate the emotional trajectory: Grayson is being systematically dismantled by Dr. Sinclair's logic, leading to a defensive, cornered state. I should have assigned a higher score to "Worried" (fear of being exposed or losing credibility) or "Inferior" (feeling intellectually outmatched), and significantly lowered "Justified" and "Triumphant" since he is losing the argument. I will ensure the scores reflect the character's defensive retreat rather than a perceived victory.
